title: SLO-driven adaptive admission with token redispatch across regions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: In recent incidents we observed single-region rate-limiter outages and degraded heuristics that caused either excessive customer throttling or uncontrolled latency spikes during burst events. Existing failover is coarse (route-all-to-remote) which breaks tenant fairness and violates tenant SLO budgets. Goal: implement an SLO-driven adaptive admission controller that can redispatch token credits across regions with hedged allocation, local-first preference, and graceful degradation when limiter nodes are degraded or partitioned. This ticket covers design, prototype, rollout and runbook updates.
acceptance_criteria: New admission controller can redirect up to 30% of burst traffic to a warm remote region within 200ms median additional latency without exceeding remote region SLOs.
System maintains tenant-level fairness: no tenant receives >20% more admitted tokens than proportional weight in steady-state across failover windows.
Limiter outage scenarios (node crash, partition, high error rate) are automatically detected and admission is adjusted within two control intervals (<=10s) with documented metrics emitted.
End-to-end integration tests exercising node crash and inter-region network delay included in CI; at least one synthetic canary passes for a week before full rollout.
Runbook updated with playbook steps for degraded limiter recovery, manual override, and emergency quota reconciliation.
Telemetry: per-tenant admitted/denied counts, redispatch rate, hedging attempts, remote-saturation signals, and SLO loss estimate emitted to Metrics and traced for 90d.
Feature flag gating and gradual rollout plan validated in staging and one canary region before enabling globally.
technical_notes: Controller model: continuous controller that observes per-tenant short-window SLO burn rates (error/latency) and adjusts admission multipliers. Controller runs in each region but coordinates via compact heartbeats and optional gossip for global state.

Token redispatch: when local admission cannot satisfy bursts, controller issues 'hedged credits' that reserve proportional capacity in remote region(s). Hedged credits are timed-license tokens with TTL and idempotent claim semantics to avoid double-admit.

Fairness guarantees: use proportional-share allocation formula where admitted_i = min(local_capacity_i, alpha * target_share_i) and remote_claims are bounded by remote_budget * tenant_weight_fraction.

Failure detection: Bayesian success-rate estimator and latency EWMA detect degraded limiter instances. High error-rate or >40% increase in p95 token processing latency triggers local soft-stop and redispatch window.

Backpressure signals: remote region emits saturation hints (saturation_score) that decrement hedged credit issuance. If remote_saturation > 0.7, controller falls back to token-drop preference for low-priority tenants.
Data plane hooks: proxy layers must add trace headers for hedged-credit id and claim path. Runtime will expose claim result codes for observability and tracing.
Compatibility: design compatible with Dedicated tenants (respect isolation rings); Dedicated tenants can opt-out of cross-region redispatch via tenant config in Account Service.
Security: all cross-region claim RPCs authenticated with mTLS and include tenant-consent token. No sensitive data flows in claims — only tenant id, requested tokens, and trace id.

Tradeoffs: Adding hedged credits increases complexity in admission path and requires careful TTL tuning to prevent token leakage. We prefer short TTLs (100-500ms) for hedged credits and strong reconciliation periodically.

Implementation milestones: (a) admission controller prototype (local-only), (b) hedged-credit claim protocol and remote acceptance, (c) fairness enforcement and audit logs, (d) metrics and CI chaos tests.
rollout_plan: Feature behind 3-tier feature flag: controller_enabled (region), hedged_redispatch (global), tenant_cross_region_allowed (tenant-level).
Stage 0: Unit + integration tests in CI; end-to-end simulation harness for 10K tenants with realistic burst traces (from incident replay).
Stage 1: Canary in staging cluster for 48h; run chaos tests (random limiter node kill, 100-200ms inter-region latency).
Stage 2: Canary in low-traffic production region (eu-west-1) for 7 days with monitoring alarms. If no regressions, enable hedged_redispatch for 5% of tenants globally for another 7 days.
Stage 3: Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% over three 48h windows, evaluating fairness and remote_saturation metrics at each stage.
Stage 4: Full global enable after 2 weeks with ops approval and docs updated.
test_plan: Unit tests for admission multiplier math and hedged-credit TTL semantics.
Integration tests: simulate cross-region claims with network partitions and ensure idempotency (claim retries not double-counting).
Chaos tests: limiter node crash, partial packet loss, and high tail latency injected via Jepsen-like harness.
Load test: synthetic tenants replaying production spike traces; validate admitted vs denied ratios and SLO burn over 1h windows.
Canary test: two tenants with drastically different weights to validate proportional fairness during redispatch windows.
CI check: run synthetic 'token leak' reconciliation scenario verifying all hedged tokens either consumed or reclaimed within 5s.
monitoring_and_runbook: New metrics: limiter.local_admit_rate, limiter.remote_redispatch_rate, limiter.hedge_claim_latency_ms, limiter.remote_saturation_score, tenant.slo_estimate_loss.
Dashboards: per-region heatmap showing redispatch traffic, top tenants by redispatch volume, and remote saturation over time.
Alerts: P1 if remote_saturation_score > 0.8 for >2m AND redispatch_rate > 5% traffic; P0 critical if admission controller errors >1% of requests over 5m.
Runbook snippet: steps to isolate failing limiter node, force-local-only mode, re-run token reconciliation, and manually adjust tenant multipliers. Link to Confluence runbook provided in links.
Manual rollback: Flip hedged_redispatch to off and set controller_enabled to off per region to revert to legacy admission in under 2 minutes.
Post-incident: capture admitted/denied traces for impacted tenants and run reconciliation job to audit hedged-token residue.
